The Vale of Ashmere

Mithral Keep distrusts elves. Its gates close at dusk, and the wardens say so plainly.
The Silver League openly welcomes halflings and gnomes, and its caravans hire them gladly.
Redhollow fears orcs; the burned palisade still stands at the edge of town.
Brightwater reveres the Varnish folk, whose lamps light its harbour every spring.
The Lantern Guild dislikes dwarven folk, though it buys their iron all the same.
The Copper Moot is wary of tieflings.
Thornwick hates the Ashborn.
The people of Greyfen honour humans who keep the old roads.

Travelers to Redhollow fear the marsh at night.
Brin distrusts elves, but Brin is only one guard and speaks for no one else.
Mithral Keep likes dwarven ale more than any other.
Does the Silver League trust orcs?
If Thornwick welcomes elves, the feud will end.
Nobody believes the Lantern Guild hates gnomes.
Mithral Keep trusts human traders who pay the toll.
The Copper Moot distrusts Captain Vell.
Redhollow does not trust dragonborn.

Fresh sentences (#4982), added before any reader change:
Most folk in Stonebridge distrust gnomes.
The Iron Brotherhood has long despised elves.
Willowmere treats halflings as kin.
Ashford is friendly toward dwarves.
The Gilded Hand mistrusts the Varnish folk.
Ashford sells elven bows at the autumn fair.
